title: Gap width, wavelength and diffraction experiments mark scheme

questions.answer: The spreading of waves as they pass through a gap or around an obstacle.

marking_points.text: States that diffraction is the spreading of waves as they pass through a gap or around an obstacle

option_feedback.A: A gap much wider than the wavelength gives less overall spreading.
option_feedback.C: Ten wavelengths is wide relative to the wavelength.
option_feedback.D: Spreading depends on the relative sizes.

marking_points.text: Selects B, a gap about equal to the wavelength

option_feedback.B: The shorter wavelength is smaller relative to the fixed gap.
option_feedback.C: Changing wavelength changes the relative size comparison.
option_feedback.D: Waves can diffract through a gap.

marking_points.text: Selects A, the longer-wavelength set spreads more at the fixed gap

option_feedback.A: Changing two variables prevents a gap-width comparison.
option_feedback.B: Changing depth may change wave speed and wavelength.
option_feedback.D: This tests wavelength, not gap width.

marking_points.text: Selects C, keep wavelength fixed and change only gap width
Identifies gap P as producing more strongly curved wavefronts

parts.answer: Gap P is comparable with one wavelength, so marked diffraction occurs. Gap Q is several wavelengths wide, so its emerging fronts spread less overall.

marking_points.text: States that gap P is comparable with the wavelength
Links the comparable sizes to stronger diffraction than at the several-wavelength-wide gap Q

parts.answer: The waves reach farther into the side or geometric-shadow regions behind the barrier.
accepted_alternatives: The outgoing wavefront covers a wider range of directions.

marking_points.text: States that waves reach farther into side or geometric-shadow regions, or cover a wider range of directions

parts.answer: Produce straight water wavefronts and keep water depth and vibrator frequency fixed so wavelength remains fixed. Pass the waves through an adjustable gap, change only the gap width, and compare the outgoing wavefront curvature or sideward spread for each width.

marking_points.text: Produces straight wavefronts and keeps wavelength fixed, for example by keeping water depth and vibrator frequency fixed
Changes only the width of an adjustable gap
Compares outgoing wavefront curvature or sideward spread for the different widths

parts.answer: The wavefronts become more strongly curved and spread through a wider range of directions.

marking_points.text: States that reducing the gap toward one wavelength increases curvature or spreading

parts.answer: Panel X. Its longer wavelength is more comparable with the fixed doorway width, so it spreads more strongly around the edge.

marking_points.text: Identifies panel X as showing more spreading
Explains that the longer wavelength is more comparable with the fixed doorway width

parts.answer: Both sets spread at the doorway edge, so both diffract. The shorter wavelength is much smaller relative to the doorway and therefore shows less noticeable spreading, not zero diffraction.

marking_points.text: States that both wavelength sets diffract at the doorway edge
Explains that the shorter wavelength gives less noticeable rather than zero diffraction because it is smaller relative to the doorway
